name: Inverse rule with a phase (IV)
summary: A Z-state with any phase α plugged into a phase-free X-effect, next to a Z- and X-spider connected by three wires, is the empty diagram.
description:
A Z-spider with phase $\alpha$ connected to a phase-free X-spider represents the scalar $\sqrt2$ for every $\alpha$, and a phase-free Z- and X-spider connected by three wires represent $\frac1{\sqrt2}$, so together they are the empty diagram. In particular the first scalar does not depend on $\alpha$.

In older axiomatisations the inverse rule (IV) appears without the phase. Vilmart showed that the version with an arbitrary phase $\alpha$, together with the [Euler rule with a Hadamard](../euler-angles-hadamard/), can replace the Euler decomposition of the Hadamard, the [Euler-angle rule](../euler-angles/) and the [Clifford+T scalar rule (E)](../clifford-t-scalar/), giving a complete axiomatisation of the universal ZX-calculus with only seven rules.
